_about: The Common Subjects Reference's procedures: one per card of the tab's Progress view, each a rule in plain words with who set it and when, what it reads, who owns it and how often it runs. canonical_subj4.js draws them under the Progress view's parts, kb/_build_commons_status.py reads their names for the Commons row, and a session reads this file before working the reference. To add one, write its words and source; to turn one off, set on to false. Lane state: docs/reference/lanes/common-subjects-reference.md.

procedures.name: Keep the MQ discipline list current
procedures.status: half built: a quarterly runner compares the edition and the handbook PDF's hash with kb/reference/csr_quarterly_baseline.json and reads red on a change (S433, csr-quarterly.yml); the index diff and the card stay a session's step
procedures.owner: a runner, then a card for Sam
procedures.rule: The discipline names come from the Chancellor's Office Minimum Qualifications handbook's Disciplines Index and nowhere else. Each quarter a runner fetches the handbook's page, records the edition and the date, and compares the index with the committed list; a change opens a card for Sam and the routine applies nothing. Every MQ discipline that carries courses on the map carries one Common SUBJ; a discipline with no courses carries none until its first course appears, and the mint path then takes the code from this reference.
steps: Fetch the handbook page on cccco.edu (https://www.cccco.edu/About-Us/Chancellors-Office/Divisions/Educational-Services-and-Support/What-we-do/Educational-Programs-and-Professional-Development/Minimum-Qualifications/, which lists the 19th edition on 2026-10-20) from a runner and record the edition, the date and a hash of the Disciplines Index.
Compare the index with kb/reference/mq_disciplines.json and kb/reference/mq_sections.json; list added, removed and renamed titles.
A change opens a card on the standing sheet with the diff; a session applies what Sam rules through the fan-in alias file or a seed edit, never a blind overwrite.
Correct the eight names that carry a Title 5 section number from the PDF extraction and the one truncated name once Sam confirms the handbook's spelling.

source.words: Keep current MQ Discipline list (quarterly scrape routine needed) ... Ensure every MQD has at least 1 Subject assigned to it

procedures.name: Keep the C-ID and CCN subject tables current
procedures.status: to build: a quarterly refresh on a runner
procedures.rule: The C-ID subject codes come from c-id.net's final descriptors and the CCN subject codes from the COCI extract's Common Course Number column. Each quarter a runner refreshes both reference files and rebuilds the attribution table; where the two authorities name the same subject differently, CCN wins.
steps: Refresh kb/reference/cid_descriptors.json from the c-id.net descriptor export and kb/reference/ccn_courses.json from the COCI Summary's Common Course Number column, on a runner.
Rebuild kb/reference/authority_subject_codes.json with kb/_seed_authority_codes.py, which attributes every code to a discipline from the promotions evidence and the rulings.
List the codes the refresh added or retired; a new four-letter authority code for a discipline on a CSR code is a re-key candidate under the authority rule and goes to a card.
Where a CCN code and a C-ID code differ for one subject, the CCN code is the Common SUBJ and the C-ID code rides the chip.

source.words: Keep current unique table of C-ID Subjects and CCN Subjects (quarterly scrape routine needed) ... Procedure to reconcile any discrepancy between CID and CCN Subjects; and 2026-09-03, item 15: Yes, CCN wins

procedures.name: The authority's code sets the Common SUBJ
procedures.status: in force since the recode of 2026-09-03
procedures.cadence: at every mint and every re-seed
procedures.owner: the mint path and the post-apply chain
procedures.rule: A discipline takes the CCN code when one exists; otherwise the C-ID code when it is four letters; otherwise its own four-letter code with the authority's code on a chip, hyphens removed. New M-IDs are minted under the discipline's code. A code this reference minted stays only where no authority code covers the subject.
steps: At a mint, kb/_seed_coci_minted_mids.py keys the new identity under the discipline's Common SUBJ from kb/discipline_canonical_subj4.json; umbrella disciplines keep their per-subject codes.
After a fold or a recode, kb/_post_apply_chain.py re-seeds the reference and rebuilds the chip fields, so canonical_source flips by itself when a code changes.
A discipline whose Common SUBJ differs from a four-letter authority code for the same subject is a missed alignment; the scan reports it unless a recorded note explains the divergence.

source.words: My gut says use CCN if available; if not, stay with 4-characters and add a CID chip with the verbatim CID code showing; eliminate hyphens

procedures.name: Every M-ID carries its discipline's code
procedures.status: measured by the daily scan; strays are re-key evidence
procedures.owner: the scan, then a re-mint under the playbook
procedures.rule: Every minted M-ID carries its discipline's Common SUBJ or one of the umbrella codes its discipline declares. The daily scan lists every other code with the identities under it. A stray is re-keyed under the re-mint playbook, with a dry run, an alias map and one cron window, never by hand, and the alias chain resolves the old key afterward.
steps: Read every minted identity in kb/coci_minted_courses.json and kb/coci_minted_singletons.json and group the codes: a discipline's Common SUBJ, a declared umbrella code, or a stray.
A stray whose identities carry a discipline is a re-key to that discipline's code; a stray with no discipline waits on the discipline-blank worklist first.
Stage the re-key as evidence (kb/_subj4_dryrun.py), register the alias map, and land it in one cron window under docs/coursecontrolnumber_remint.md.

source.words: Check unique table of M-ID Subjects against C-ID and CCN Subjects to eliminate unnecessary M-ID minted Subjects and reassign to appropriate CID or CCN Subject

procedures.name: One code, one MQ discipline
procedures.status: measured by the daily scan and the tab's own check
procedures.rule: One code belongs to one MQ discipline. The exceptions are the umbrella disciplines, whose codes are declared on the entry, and a fan-in pair both entries declare. A code two disciplines share otherwise is a collision: the scan reports it and a curator settles it on the tab or on a card.
steps: The scan's uniqueness rule reports a code on two disciplines, a mutual fan-in excepted.
The tab's check lists the collisions, the rows off their canonical and the disciplines with no code, with a word that jumps to each row.
A collision is settled by giving one discipline another code or by moving the mis-filed identities; the change is a re-key under the playbook.

source.words: Ensure that all Subjects are assigned an MQD; each Common SUBJ belongs to exactly one discipline, collision-free

procedures.name: Umbrellas, fan-ins and cross-listed courses
procedures.status: in force; the cross-list lane carries the open rows
procedures.cadence: at every fold and every re-discipline
procedures.owner: a session under the playbook, Sam on the cross-list sheet
procedures.rule: An umbrella discipline splits its codes by the subject a student enrolls in and keeps its MQ name: Foreign Languages, Kinesiology, Agriculture and Agricultural Production. A fan-in folds two MQ names for one field to one name and keeps the other as an alias: Kinesiology and Physical Education, Drama/Theater Arts and Theater Arts, Ethnic Studies and its two empty siblings. A course with two real homes keeps one primary discipline and carries the second as a cross-list. A subject code of one or two characters never decides a discipline alone.
steps: Read the shape first: one MQ name over many enrollment subjects is an umbrella (split the codes); two MQ names for one field is a fan-in (fold the names, keep the alias).
Declare an umbrella's codes on its entry and a fan-in on both entries, so the scan and the mint path read the exception from the file.
A course whose member colleges disagree about its discipline goes through the cross-list lane's four kinds; a defect from a short code is gated, a genuine dual home is cross-listed.

procedures.name: A person confirms each pick; a procedure may confirm the authority's own
procedures.status: in force since 2026-10-19 (Sam, Open Asks Sheet 99 card 2): the nightly run confirms the authority's own; a person confirms the rest
procedures.cadence: at every save; nightly at 08:17 UTC
procedures.owner: a curator on the tab; the nightly run under csr-confirm-authority@bot
procedures.rule: A pick is confirmed when a person sets or accepts it on the tab. The nightly procedure confirms a pick whose code equals the authority's own, CCN or C-ID, and that no finding holds back, under the cohort csr-confirm-authority@bot, insert-only with a committed receipt, so a person's time goes to the picks no authority settles. A pick on a code this reference minted waits for a person.
steps: A curator sets the Common SUBJ cell on the tab; the save writes the pick to kb_curation and the daily sync carries it into the seed.

csr-confirm.yml runs kb/_csr_confirm_authority.py nightly at 08:17 UTC, after the daily run has re-synced the seed and re-run the scan: it lists the unconfirmed picks whose code is the CCN subject code or one of the C-ID subject codes and that no finding names, except the two that corroborate (the unconfirmed state itself, and the alignment the pick rests on).

A fresh read of the live picks first: a live code row for the discipline, whoever wrote it, holds the save. The receipt under kb/csr_out/confirm/ is written before the insert, the insert ignores duplicates, and the receipt then names what landed and what was held.
python3 kb/_csr_confirm_authority.py --undo takes the cohort's rows back in one delete and clears the seed's stamps. A pick on a code this reference minted waits for a person, as before.

procedures.name: The daily scan, Jev's sitting, then a card
procedures.status: the scan runs daily from this change; Jev sits on dispatch
procedures.owner: the daily run; Jev; Sam on a card
procedures.rule: The scan runs daily, read-only, and writes its findings beside the identity codes: the format, uniqueness, squatting, alignment, modal, mnemonic, hygiene, wiring and anchor rules. A finding that needs a judgment goes to Jev's sitting and then to a card for Sam; a recorded note settles a divergence, and the scan stops asking.
steps: daily-dashboard.yml runs kb/_csr_trail.py --latest after the daily sync and before the Commons status build; the Progress view and the Commons row read kb/csr_out/latest.json.
A session runs the scan without the flag for a dated receipt under kb/csr_out/<date>/ before a sitting or a re-key.
Jev's sitting (kb/_jev_adjudicate.py through typesafe-smoke.yml) reads the askable findings; what it cannot settle goes to the standing sheet.
